headline: Contrastive Discovery reports more resolved questions under matched experimental budgets
summary: The authors introduce Contrastive Discovery, a way for scientific discovery agents to evaluate a question against several competing explanations rather than one focal hypothesis and its unstructured negation. On six scientific and social datasets, they report 161.9 resolved questions at top-K 200 versus 97.2 for pointwise surprisal (+67%) under the same 200 experimental validations. A blinded study with 38 experts reports agreement on 78% of resolved questions. The results are author-reported and use GPT-4o-based discovery and belief-elicitation agents; two higher-cost datasets have one run each, no independent reproduction was performed, and the method may omit the explanation best supported by evidence. The paper does not establish external generality or validated scientific discoveries. The authors also report that an external-evaluator audit found fewer structurally complete contrast sets than the same-provider evaluator, and that deliberately omitted supported explanations caused frequent wrong resolutions without abstention; this stress test does not estimate the natural omission rate.
